title: Compare integrated counted Balanced with qsvlite and DuckDB
question: How does the integrated opt-in build with the approved fingerprint change compare on the out-of-memory 8 GiB Balanced fixture?
summary: Integrated Chopper median 38.87 s, qsvlite 22.53 s, ordered materialized DuckDB adapter 66.84 s. Independent paired ablation attributes about 4.6 CPU s to removed fingerprint work.

workloads: 8 GiB plain CSV, eight exact consecutive parts, hard 1 GiB cgroup without swap and one worker.

validation.summary: Three verified rotating measured rounds after one complete warmup per tool. Independent full CSV output, order, quotas, caps, and Chopper publication/cleanup checks.

limitations: WSL2/ext4 with uncontrolled backing cache. Input exceeds the cgroup and fits host RAM. Scope excludes native Windows.
qsvlite sequential split and DuckDB materialize-and-slice are specific adapters. The divisible fixture yields exact quotas in all three.
The opt-in Chopper build includes the approved fingerprint change. The separate 40 GiB qualification predates this change.
exclusions: Three warmups. Fixture preparation and identity, cache eviction advice, and independent verification outside the timed commands.
